query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing approximately 0.5 at% interstitial carbon into (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 will enhance its load-bearing integrity by means of solid-solution strengthening without significantly altering the caloric phase transformation that gives rise to its large caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but suffers from poor load-bearing integrity and cracking.
generation.intervention: Add a low-level interstitial carbon doping (~0.5 at% C) during synthesis of the alloy.
generation.conditions: Operated under refrigeration conditions with the same applied magnetic and pressure fields and at temperatures near the caloric transformation range as the undoped alloy.
generation.structural_mediator: Interstitial carbon atoms occupying sites within the alloy matrix, leading to solid-solution strengthening.
generation.mechanism: The carbon atoms, when introduced in low concentration, occupy octahedral interstitial sites in the lattice and restrict dislocation motion. This increases yield strength and fracture toughness (improving load-bearing integrity) while having minimal impact on the phase balance and energetics that enable the caloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: The carbon-doped alloy is predicted to exhibit improved mechanical properties—such as higher yield strength and reduced crack propagation—while maintaining a similar magnitude of caloric response (e.g., similar entropy change under field and pressure cycling) as compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.baseline: The undoped (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, which shows a strong caloric effect but is compromised by poor load-bearing performance and susceptibility to cracking.
generation.boundary: This improvement is expected to hold under refrigeration-operating conditions, where the alloy is cycled through the conventional temperature, applied-field, pressure-field, and mechanical loading regimes used in solid refrigeration.
generation.uncertainty: The precise carbon concentration that optimally balances mechanical strengthening with minimal interference of the caloric phase transformation requires further optimization; slight shifts in transformation temperature or response magnitude may occur and must be quantified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one of the standard (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy and one doped with ~0.5 at% carbon. Subject both sets to identical mechanical tests (compression, bending, fracture toughness measurements) and assess the caloric performance by measuring field-induced entropy changes and transformation temperatures under applied magnetic and pressure fields within the refrigeration temperature range.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the carbon-doped alloy does not show a statistically significant improvement in load-bearing integrity compared to the control, or if the caloric response (magnitude or transformation temperature) deviates significantly from that of the undoped alloy beyond experimental uncertainty, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

reading.lever: Introduce a low-level interstitial C doping into (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 to enhance matrix strength without altering caloric phase transformation.
reading.why: This approach, proven in related HEAs, offers solid-solution strengthening and improved load-bearing integrity while minimally impacting the caloric response.
